content.comment_body: Hello, could someone assist with my issue? I'm trying to connect to a [company_name] [product_name] [article_no]. I've written my first program and purchased the related software, which came with a green Ethernet cable. I plugged the cable into both my laptop and the [product_name], but when I attempt to transfer my program, an information box appears saying, "IP Address of your PC and the target [product_name] are not in the same subnet. The application tries to add an additional local IP Address, do you want to continue?" I'm unsure how to proceed to communicate with the [product_name] and upload my program. Any help in guiding me would be appreciated. Thank you, [user_name]

Welcome [user_name]. The address of your [product_name] consists of two components—IP address and subnet mask. Your PC should have a distinct IP address but stay within the same range. For example: [product_name] IP - 192.168.0.1, subnet mask - 255.255.255.0. Where the subnet mask is 255, your PC’s IP address numbers must match, except the last part, which can be any number besides '1', already used by the [product_name]. So: PC IP - 192.168.0.x, subnet mask - 255.255.255.0; where x can be any number except 1. Please search online for instructions on setting a fixed IP address for your PC, and be sure to note your changes for later.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experiences difficulties connecting their PC to a [company_name] [product_name] using Ethernet. The main issue stems from incompatible IP and subnet settings between their PC and the device, resulting in a confusing system prompt and hindering communication. This situation indicates a need for clearer instructions or more user-friendly diagnostics in the software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates an easy setup and smooth connection between their PC and the [product_name], hoping to upload programs without requiring advanced networking expertise.
